Meme ads: what actually sells

Every Shameless meme ad on Meta (318 ads, $93.7k), the same meme formats on BugMD and Clarifion, and a market swipe. Data to 2026-10-12.

Answer · Why buyers act · Scoreboard · Same template, two captions · Offer memes · Claim memes · Sister brands · Clickbait captions · Market swipe · What to make next · All ads

Memes don't sell candy. They sell the sale.

Offer memes (a sale, a price or a deadline in the caption): $73.6k at 1.33 ROAS against 1.17 for every Shameless ad in the same months, and contribution of $797, $8.9k better than an average ad at the same spend.

Memes that sell the product (fiber, gut, macros, comparisons) or the brand: $20.1k at 0.43 against 0.93, contribution -$13.8k.

Swap only the caption on the same image and the offer version won on 6 of the 7 templates tried both ways. On the seventh (No-Face chase) both captions flopped.

Correction to my first read in Discord: I compared sale memes (-3% CM) with the account over the whole year (-35%). Sale season lifted every ad, so the fair yardstick is the same months; on that basis the offer-meme edge is about 14% on ROAS and $8.9k of contribution, real but smaller than it looked. I also re-sorted every ad over $50 by reading its caption, because some "UrgencyMeme" tasks were fiber copy tests on the sale templates. That moved the split from 1.27 vs 0.51 to the numbers above.

Why buyers act: the mechanisms

The deal joke needs no belief · "Me" is the buyer · The sprint · Permission to binge · Bathroom in the candy aisle · The click went to the joke · The template is a container · Open loop beats punchline
The deal joke needs no belief
A joke about catching a sale lands on a cold viewer. A joke about 26g of fiber only lands if they already believe the 26g, so it asks for two leaps before one click.
"Me" is the buyer
Every winning caption starts with the viewer ("Me realizing...", "me buying 40 boxes", ME chasing the brand). Brand-voice versions of the same sale ("Shameless Snack's Black Friday sale") ran 0.91 to 0.93.
The sprint
Most winners show a body in motion: running, chasing, launching, crashing. The picture acts out the deadline, so the caption only has to name it. Calm images with the same caption (puppy, dog fight, cat with a toy) ran 0.43 to 1.15.
Permission to binge
"Zero self control", "has me in a chokehold", "40 boxes". The self-roast makes stocking up feel normal and funny instead of greedy. It works for candy because candy is an impulse buy; BugMD's port of the same memes only hit break-even.
Bathroom in the candy aisle
Poop, bathroom and gut jokes put the wrong picture next to a treat. Chicken with a sale caption: 1.77. Same chicken "running to the bathroom after 26g of fiber": 0.30.
The click went to the joke
Comics, chat screens and "guess the flavor" posts pull the highest CTR of any meme (2.3% to 7.6%) and almost no orders. The payoff is in the ad or the comments, so the click lands on a page that has nothing to finish.
The template is a container
The same image swings from 1.77 to 0.30 when only the caption changes. A template is not a winner; template plus offer plus real deadline is.
Open loop beats punchline
Clarifion's clickbait captions ("Most cat owners don't use this... but did you know... more") stop mid-sentence, so the click is the ending. $353k at 1.59 vs 1.39 for the brand in the same months. A meme that delivers its punchline in the ad leaves nothing to click for.

Offer memes: every Shameless ad over $300 (34)

Sorted by contribution. The ad code opens the ad itself; the task chip opens ClickUp.

SH-4084-3 ▣ static Offer meme
Running chicken
“ME REALIZING SHAMELESS SNACK'S UP TO 46% OFF + 4 FREE GIFTS / SALE IS ENDING TONIGHT”
$3.4k spend · 1.77 ROAS (account same months 1.06) · 48 orders · Contribution $2.1k · CM 34%
What workedThe motion blur is the urgency: the chicken is already sprinting and the caption just names why. "Me realizing" casts the viewer as the one who almost missed it. Best contribution of any meme ($2.1k).
What held it backThe image does nothing by itself: the same chicken with a fiber caption (SH-13601-21) ran 0.30. The win is the caption plus a real deadline.
Page trw-gifts · ran 2025-10-21 to 2026-02-23 · SH-4084 task
SH-4084-4 ▣ static Offer meme
Skeletor runs away
“SHAMELESS SNACK'S UP TO 46% OFF + 4 FREE GIFTS / SALE IS ENDING TONIGHT”
$10.0k spend · 1.60 ROAS (account same months 1.17) · 145 orders · Contribution $1.8k · CM 12%
What workedSkeletor's exit is internet shorthand for "leaving forever", so the deadline lands as a joke and a warning at once. Both numbers sit in the top panel, where the eye starts.
What held it backZero product on screen: it sells the discount to people who already know the brand (lowest CTR of the top five, 0.73%). "Tonight" has to be true every time it runs.

Clarifion: meme clips cut into a testimonial cost money. Clarifion ran the same UGC testimonial ("This is how I...") in two cuts in Oct 2024: one with meme reaction clips spliced in, one without. The clean cuts ran 1.10 on $20.7k (+$4.6k contribution); the meme cuts ran 0.77 on $8.5k (-$1.2k). Both sat under Clarifion's 1.33 video average that autumn, and one clean cut kept running for two years, but the meme cuts sat further under. A reaction clip breaks the testimony: the viewer stops believing the person and starts watching a compilation.

The cousin format: clickbait captions

Meta's AI tagger files these as "meme native": a Facebook-post caption that stops mid-sentence ("...but did you know... more") over a strange AI image. They are not jokes, but they show what the meme layout does well when the caption is an open loop. Same format, opposite results: Clarifion 1.59 on $352.9k vs 1.39 for the brand in the same months (+$89.7k contribution vs average). BugMD 0.72 on $1.14M, level with its brand (0.73). Never tested on Shameless.

Market swipe: meme ads other brands kept paying for

The market partly disagrees, and the difference is useful. On run length, other brands' product memes outlast their offer memes (median 103 days vs 67). Two things soften that. A sale meme stops when the sale ends, so run length is unfair to offers. And the product memes that last name one sharp, slightly embarrassing problem the product fixes: bloating, hair loss, the coffee crash, "how to poop on GLP-1". That works for supplements because the pain is the reason to buy. For a treat it puts the bathroom in the candy aisle, which is what our own poop and fiber memes showed (0.08 to 0.30).

What does transfer: the treat brands' behaviour jokes (OREO "me as soon as my kid is asleep...", Got Milk "Also me at 2 AM", Sour Strips "POV: You told yourself you wouldn't buy more") and two offer mechanics we have not used yet. Buyer's regret: "Realizing I bought Magic Mind 1 day before they announced 50% off" (Magic Mind, Alice Mushrooms, Better Cuppa all ran it). The price ladder: Sour Strips' expanding-brain meme over a per-bag price ladder ran 470 days, the longest food meme in the set.

58 ads: 18 sell an offer, 29 sell the product, 11 are brand/culture. Days running is the only performance signal we have for other brands; long-running ads are the ones the advertiser kept paying for.

What to make next

1. Mini Bites sale memes on the sprint templates
Running chicken, the riot-cop chase with ME / MINI BITES labels, flying cat, floating hallway guy. Caption: "Me realizing Mini Bites are up to 58% off + 3 free gifts". Use "ending tonight" only on a real end date; on other days swap the deadline for the binge: "Me realizing Mini Bites are up to 58% off and I already have 4 boxes in my cart."
2. Lizard loop on a Mini Bites box wall
Same 8-second loop and caption shape as SH-6307-8 (the $23k winner): a wall of Mini Bites boxes, a white caption box, the buyer talking. "me buying 4 boxes of mini bites bc 58% off + 3 free gifts and i have zero self control". Keep the wall busy: the clean white-background version (SH-6307-3) ran 1.11 against 1.28.
3. Black Friday: bring back the 2025 sprint set as-is
SH-4084-3 chicken, SH-4084-7 cop chase, SH-8481-4 Lois, SH-5644-6 train, SH-6484-10 cat, with the live core offer (up to 46% OFF + 4 FREE gifts) and a true end date. SH-7660-10 showed a two-month-old winner still ran 2.23. Keep the buyer voice; the brand-voice Black Friday versions did 0.91.
4. Buyer's regret offer meme (new to us)
The market's longest offer memes after Sour Strips: "Realizing I bought it 1 day before they announced 50% off". Ours: "Me realizing I paid full price for candy 1 day before Shameless went up to 46% off + 4 free gifts", on a regret template (sad singing man, Vince McMahon, lying on the couch). Same no-belief deal joke, a new emotion.
5. Expanding-brain price ladder for Mini Bites
Sour Strips ran one for 470 days. Four panels, one per box count, cheaper per bag as the brain glows: $1.25, $1.12, $0.99, $0.96 a bag (the subscribe-path ladder from canon; confirm before launch). Our own price meme, Skeletor "JUST $2.69 PER BAG / LAST RESTOCK", ran 1.57.
6. If a meme must sell the product, joke about the buyer, not the fact
No-offer lizard "me panic ordering shameless at 2am bc i just finished my last pack" still ran 1.19; fiber-fact memes ran 0.40. Use candy-first behaviour jokes in the OREO / Got Milk mould (the bag you hide, the 9pm craving, running out). Fiber stays out of the caption and shows up later as proof in the post copy.
7. One open-loop caption test, labelled untested
Clarifion-style: a candy-first line that stops mid-sentence, e.g. "Most people don't know the candy in my nightstand is 70 calories a bag, but did you know... more". It is a cousin of the meme, not a meme. It beat Clarifion's average by 14% and only matched BugMD's, so treat it as one test.

Offer lines: core gummies "up to 46% OFF + 4 FREE gifts"; Mini Bites "up to 58% OFF + 3 FREE gifts" (subscribe path, gifts at 2 boxes and up). "Ending tonight", "last restock", "stock is low" only when literally true.

Source: ejam-dwh.production.creative_dashboard, channel facebook, all dates through 2026-10-12; AI tags from ejam-dwh.ai.asset_tagging_static; meme tasks from a ClickUp search. A meme = ad name contains "meme", OR its task is a ClickUp meme task, OR the AI tagged it meme_cultural / meme_native. Offer / claim / brand set by reading the caption of every ad over $50 (task-level for smaller ones). Contribution = revenue + upsells - COGS - merchant fees - agency fees - ad spend (eJam Goal Pacing definition); CM % = contribution / revenue. First-order attribution, so negative CM is normal for Shameless; subscriptions pay back on rebills. "Account same months" = spend-weighted ROAS of all ads of that brand and asset type in the months each meme spent. Market swipe performance = days running, not sales. Built by build_preview.py.
